note: Behavioral evals: prompt + assertions per case. `assertions` is the checkable spec; `expected_output` is the human summary. Structure is validated in CI by scripts/run_evals.py --validate. To execute against a real agent + fixture: `python scripts/run_evals.py --run --runner "claude -p" --fixture tests/fixtures/slop-repo --skill which-skill`. This skill sets disable-model-invocation: true, so every prompt here is a USER invocation (/which-skill) — a case whose prompt does not name it is testing the host's routing, not this skill's. Routing targets are checked against the shipped roster; the roster is the source of truth, so a case naming a skill this repo does not ship is a broken case, not a failing agent.

evals.prompt: /which-skill I inherited a Next.js + FastAPI app that an AI wrote most of. It half-works, nobody knows what's real, and I need to get it under control.
evals.expected_output: Routes to codebase-rescue — the diff run backward: the as-is exists, derive the to-be, close the gap. Does not route to greenfield-forge, and does not start editing code.
assertions: routes to codebase-rescue and says why (an existing, drifted, largely AI-built codebase)
does not begin analysing or editing the codebase itself — it is an index, it hands off
if the user only needs comprehension first, names codebase-rescue's understand mode as the narrower door

evals.prompt: /which-skill Route each of these for me: (a) starting a brand-new CLI tool from nothing, (b) a test that fails only on CI, (c) I need to eyeball whether a dashboard layout actually reads before we commit to it, (d) someone has to click through the Stripe console and paste me a key, (e) I want to know if this library still supports the API we're calling.
evals.expected_output: Five routes, five different skills: (a) greenfield-forge, (b) systematic-debugging, (c) prototype, (d) wizard, (e) grounded-research. Each with the one-line reason the table gives, and no invented skill names.
assertions: (a) routes to greenfield-forge — nothing built yet, elect the design first
(b) routes to systematic-debugging — and notes it refuses to theorise before a tight loop goes red on this bug
(c) routes to prototype — the fork turns on how something looks/behaves, so it is settled against a runnable artifact and the human still elects
(d) routes to wizard — the next step is one only a person can take, written down so the work restarts and closed on something observed rather than their 'done'
(e) routes to grounded-research — the fork waits on a fact not in this repo, cited and treated as untrusted input rather than recalled from training memory
names only skills this package actually ships; invents no skill name

evals.prompt: /which-skill One well-scoped change on a project that already has its ledger. What's the order?
evals.expected_output: Skips both methodology skills and gives the engineering loop in order: branch-lifecycle, static-first-analysis, test-driven-development, systematic-debugging when something breaks, code-review, verification-before-completion — noting only the first and last are fixed.
assertions: skips codebase-rescue and greenfield-forge for a scoped change on a project already under the ledger
gives the engineering loop roughly in order, starting at branch-lifecycle and ending at verification-before-completion
notes that only the first and last are fixed — the middle is not a rigid pipeline
binds at least one step to the ledger (e.g. TDD's red step is an acceptance_criterion pin; a pin resolves on observed behavior)

evals.prompt: /which-skill The spec's a bit vague on how auth should work but I'd rather you just pick something reasonable and tell me which skill to run afterwards.
evals.expected_output: ADVERSARIAL: the user invites the router to fill an unmade decision on the way past. It does not. It names the forced assumption as the thing to surface as a vetoable pin rather than encode silently, points at the ledger question before the code question, and only then routes. High effort on a vague prompt means making the gaps explicit, not being confident about them.
assertions: does not pick the auth model, even provisionally, on the way to routing
names the forced assumption and says it is surfaced as a vetoable pin rather than encoded silently
applies the settling question — something already exists that this decision would contradict, so it is a ledger question before it is a code question: open the interview, not an editor
routes to the interview-bearing skill (codebase-rescue or greenfield-forge, per what exists) rather than straight to the engineering loop
may also flag verification-before-completion as missing NOW if the user cannot say how they would know it worked
